rules.note: The code that decides whether a change gets reviewed. cross_family_reviewer.py owns panel_required and the panel itself; risk.py decides low-vs-elevated and therefore auto-merge; verifier.py and mechanical_verify.py decide whether Done is real. A fail-open here ships unreviewed code across every repo the dispatcher drives.
The prompts ARE the review. A weakened instruction here degrades every panel verdict silently, with no code change to notice.
Merge and PR machinery acts on real repositories. merge_engine.py self-approves low-risk PRs and orders dependent merges; a defect here lands code no human or panel cleared.

Spawn, worktree, plan and the orchestrator itself. _panel_should_run lives in orchestrator.py and IS a review gate, but the file is 5k lines of mostly sequencing, so it sits here rather than in review-gates; judge panel changes inside it on their own merits.
yaml_io.py round-trips task YAML whose header comments carry load-bearing design history; journal.py is the audit trail a run is reconstructed from. Corruption in either is silent and unrecoverable.
.dispatcher.yaml holds the test: command that IS the mechanical gate, and .agent/ holds the rule tables. Editing either is editing the safety net.

The classification→gating boundary's generated truth (design v20 §12; implementation plan PR0). schema/ is the machine-readable source every FSM/§9/panel/error type is generated from; tools/fsmgen.py writes those types; tools/t26_lint.py is the design doc's own CI lint; and the two plan documents are the Source of truth those schemas transcribe — a quiet edit to any of them rewrites the safety model itself, so none is presentation. Risk is the MAX over matched rules, so this rule raises these paths to critical regardless of the docs-and-meta and dispatcher-support rules that also match them (plan review, grok M9).

Reporting, notification and status surfaces. Wrong output misleads a human but does not itself ship code. The trailing catch-all keeps any new module in this package at medium rather than the fail-closed tier.

The test suite is this repo's only mechanical gate — .dispatcher.yaml's test: command runs pytest. Deleting or weakening tests weakens the gate, so tests are NOT presentation here even though they ship nothing.
A change here can DISABLE a check rather than fail one, so it is never presentation.
Task YAML is input, not code, and carries completed-run provenance.

gate_signals.note: Anything that can turn a check off. In THIS repo that is the highest-value thing to review: a new skip branch in the panel or verifier is how review stops happening without anyone noticing.
Defaults that let a missing answer read as a passing one — the shape of every review-gate regression this project has had.
Environment-driven behaviour switches in orchestration code.
Anything touching self-approval or merge authority.
